system_description.narrative_title: US–China tech and chip rivalry amid China's economic strain
system_description.narrative_summary: News converges on a single dominant story: accelerating strategic competition over AI and semiconductors as China tightens controls and confronts slowing domestic demand. The interaction of regulatory moves, capital-market activity (IPOs, funding rounds), supply-chain reshoring, and talent flows is reshaping investment, manufacturing location decisions and geopolitical risk perceptions. Feedbacks between economic weakness in China and tougher export/exit rules are intensifying decoupling pressures while prompting private-sector responses in chips and AI globally.
system_description.scope: The tech-industrial system linking AI development, semiconductor design and manufacturing, capital markets (IPOs, funding), regulatory and security policies (export/exit rules, national-security controls), global supply chains, and cross-border talent and data flows — with primary actors including state authorities (China, US, allied governments), major tech and chip firms, investors, and research labs.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic order (US–China strategic rivalry and the global economy)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and IPO/funding ecosystem
International manufacturing and semiconductor supply chains
Labor/talent mobility and higher education pipelines

variables.name: AI capability growth
variables.description: The pace at which general and domain-specific AI model capabilities and performance improve over time.

variables.name: Advanced semiconductor production capacity
variables.description: The installed manufacturing capacity for producing leading-node and advanced semiconductor components.

variables.name: Semiconductor technology diffusion rate
variables.description: The speed at which advanced chipmaking techniques and equipment spread across producers and locations.

variables.name: Capital inflow rate to tech
variables.description: The flow rate of equity, debt and private funding directed into technology and semiconductor development and manufacturing.

variables.name: Market sentiment toward technology sector
variables.description: The aggregate investor and market confidence and risk appetite for technology and semiconductor assets and IPOs.

variables.name: Regulatory restriction intensity
variables.description: The overall stringency of government controls on exports, foreign travel, exits, and national-security related technology measures.

variables.name: Supply-chain geographic concentration
variables.description: The degree to which critical manufacturing, assembly and materials nodes are geographically concentrated versus dispersed.

variables.name: Manufacturing reshoring rate
variables.description: The rate at which production capacity and associated activities are relocated back to domestic or allied jurisdictions.

variables.name: Cross-border talent mobility
variables.description: The flow rate of skilled researchers, engineers and technical personnel moving between countries and regions.

variables.name: Data and IP transfer restrictions
variables.description: The level of legal and practical limits on cross-border transfer of data, intellectual property and research outputs.

variables.name: Domestic demand strength
variables.description: The aggregate strength of household and business consumption and investment demand within a major domestic market.

variables.name: Technology market liquidity
variables.description: The availability of liquid capital and tradable depth for technology-sector securities and financing instruments.

variables.name: Geopolitical tension level
variables.description: The perceived intensity of strategic rivalry and political friction influencing economic and technological interactions.

variables.name: R&D collaboration rate
variables.description: The rate of cross-border joint research projects, talent exchanges and co-authored scientific outputs in advanced technologies.

variables.name: Production cost gap
variables.description: The difference in unit production costs (labor, energy, materials, compliance) between alternative manufacturing locations.

variables.name: Cyber and security incident rate
variables.description: The frequency of cyberattacks, IP thefts and security incidents that disrupt technology development or supply chains.

catalysts.title: SK Hynix–Intel US memory talks
catalysts.description: Exclusive talks to make memory chips in the U.S.; could lead to new US fabs and joint investments.
catalysts.rationale: Exclusive reports: 'SK Hynix in talks with Intel about deal to make memory chips in the US.'

catalysts.title: Japan–US $550bn chip plant talks
catalysts.description: Bilateral discussions on building chip plants under a proposed $550bn investment package could spur new capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Japan, U.S. discuss building chip plant under $550 bln investment talks.'

catalysts.title: China tightens exit/tech controls enforcement
catalysts.description: New exit restrictions and national-security tech exit rules expand enforcement, constraining overseas travel and tech mobility.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple items: 'China Tightens Exit Restrictions', 'new tech, national security exit rules take effect', 'China tightens control of overseas travel.'

catalysts.title: OpenAI pre-IPO funding round
catalysts.description: Potential large private funding round at ~$1.2tn valuation ahead of IPO could inject major capital into AI infrastructure and firms.
catalysts.rationale: Reports: 'OpenAI considers funding round at $1.2tn valuation ahead of delayed IPO.'

catalysts.title: Deployment of $22bn chip financing
catalysts.description: Banks' $22bn loan to Blackstone/Alphabet AI cloud venture is likely to fund chip capacity and infrastructure deployments.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Banks provide $22 billion chip loan to Blackstone, Alphabet AI cloud venture, source says.'

catalysts.title: Applied Materials $5bn India investment
catalysts.description: Large equipment/investment push in India tied to India's chip initiative, supporting local supply chains and capacity growth.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Applied Materials to invest $5 billion in India as Modi's flagship chip event kicks off.'

catalysts.title: High-NA EUV adoption by customers
catalysts.description: Customers embracing ASML High-NA systems accelerates adoption of leading-edge lithography, shifting tech leadership and costs.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'ASML extends chipmaking dominance as customers embrace High NA.'

catalysts.title: China push for bigger, stronger advanced manufacturing
catalysts.description: Xi's call and Beijing rhetoric could prompt directed subsidies, investment or incentives to boost domestic advanced manufacturing.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Xi calls for "bigger, stronger" advanced manufacturing sector' and China's economic weakness/investment slump.

catalysts.title: Labor crunch at U.S. chip fabs
catalysts.description: Ongoing labor shortages at U.S. fabs constrain expansion timelines and raise costs for leading-edge production.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Labor crisis in U.S. chip manufacturing leaves Samsung, TSMC desperate for talent.'

catalysts.title: China AI labs accelerate development push
catalysts.description: Public and corporate calls for faster AI development (Huawei, Xi guidance) could intensify R&D spending and capability race.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'China’s AI labs must accelerate development, says Huawei chair' and 'China Also Thinks AI Could Kill Us. But First, It Wants to Match the U.S.'
